book.title: Do Not Answer the Third Knock
book.author: Noor Hollow

lines: Grandma's rules for the village were simple.
Never step over a sleeping dog.
And when someone knocks three times at night, answer the first, ignore the second, and never, ever answer the third.
"The first is the neighbour," she said, not looking up from her beads.
"The second is the wind, wanting company.
The third is whatever has learned how to knock like the neighbour."
Last night, in the city, in my own flat, someone knocked.
Then a second knock, softer, from inside the wardrobe: the wind, I told myself, though there is no wind in a wardrobe.
I am sitting on the kitchen floor with my back against the fridge, my grandmother's beads wound round my wrist, counting.
It is the quietest I have ever heard a house.
And there, from the front door, patient and exactly in the voice of my own mother, comes the third.
